summary: Ten comment-endorsed tools, creative projects, and learning resources from the completed HN front-page crawl.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 past front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Quint
items.source_story_title: The internet discovers TLA+. Now what?
items.summary: A formal-modeling language for testing system designs before implementation; one user found transaction bugs.
items.why_included: A first-hand report describes concrete bugs caught by modeling features with Quint.
items.evidence: A commenter says their Quint-assisted design workflow found and fixed transaction and atomicity bugs, though it takes longer.

evidence_sources.author: stevefan1999
evidence_sources.excerpt: A lot of transaction and atomic bugs were found and fixed just by having such simple instruction alone.

items.name: Fakecloud
items.source_story_title: Fakecloud: Local AWS cloud emulator for integration tests
items.summary: A local AWS emulator for integration tests; a commenter praised its SES support.
items.why_included: A reply explicitly favors Fakecloud's SES support over LocalStack's.
items.evidence: One commenter says its SES support looks especially good, better than LocalStack's; this is an impression, not a test report.

evidence_sources.author: zeronone
evidence_sources.excerpt: The support for SES looks really great, better than LocalStack.

items.name: Kagi
items.source_story_title: When did Google get so weird?
items.summary: A paid search engine; a longtime user likes its results and customer-first model.
items.why_included: A multi-year user offers direct positive experience, with another commenter praising its search-first assistant.
items.evidence: One user says they have used Kagi for years without looking back; another calls its search-first assistant great.

evidence_sources.author: kelnos
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using Kagi for a couple years now and haven't looked back.

evidence_sources.author: terribleperson
evidence_sources.excerpt: Searching first is how Kagi assistant works and it's great.

items.name: Plash
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Lofi Cities – Pixel-art city nights with browser-generated lofi
items.summary: A macOS app for using websites as desktop wallpapers; tested with Lofi Cities.
items.why_included: A commenter reports a specific working setup rather than speculative compatibility.
items.evidence: A user tested Lofi Cities as a macOS wallpaper in Plash and reports that it works well.

evidence_sources.author: andelink
evidence_sources.excerpt: Just tested and this works great on macOS with Plash [1] by Sindre Sorhus.

items.name: Cindori Backdrop
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Lofi Cities – Pixel-art city nights with browser-generated lofi
items.summary: A paid macOS live-wallpaper app; a user reports good results with it.
items.why_included: The comment supplies a direct positive use report and the product's own URL.
items.evidence: A commenter reports great success with Cindori Backdrop while noting it is not free.

evidence_sources.author: Vakaiser
evidence_sources.excerpt: While it's not free or a first party offering, I've had great success with Cindori Backdrop:

items.name: Lofi Cities
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Lofi Cities – Pixel-art city nights with browser-generated lofi
items.summary: Browser-based pixel-city scenes with procedurally synthesized lofi music; commenters praised the presentation.
items.why_included: Independent replies praise the city's presentation and the FM-synth music.
items.evidence: One commenter calls the site gorgeous and well executed; another praises its FM synthesizer sound.

evidence_sources.author: bitwize
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love the FM synth in the music.

items.name: TinyAIArena
items.source_story_title: Show HN: TinyAIArena watch AI agents battle it out
items.summary: A site for watching AI agents battle; a commenter liked the experience and aesthetic.
items.why_included: The reply explicitly praises the project, rather than merely describing its launch.
items.evidence: A commenter says they love the project and its aesthetic.

evidence_sources.author: rao-v
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love this and the aesthetic.

items.name: Optimizing software in C++
items.summary: Agner Fog's freely available C++ optimization PDF; a commenter flagged it as promising.
items.why_included: The reply names a concrete free resource and positively recommends its apparent relevance.
items.evidence: A commenter calls the PDF a great-looking resource, but explicitly says they have not read it.

evidence_sources.author: MaxBarraclough
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've not read Fog's Optimizing software in C++ but I see it's freely available there as a PDF (182 pages). Looks like a great resource on these topics.

items.name: Leslie Lamport's TLA+ video course
items.source_story_title: The internet discovers TLA+. Now what?
items.summary: A TLA+ video course taught by Leslie Lamport; recommended as an approachable introduction.
items.why_included: A commenter independently points readers to the course and praises it.
items.evidence: A commenter calls Lamport's TLA+ course lovely, with memorable presentation.

evidence_sources.author: drpacman
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is a lovely little course on TLA+ by Lamport himself - has some great wigs too

items.name: You're probably using the wrong dictionary
items.source_story_title: When did Google get so weird?
items.summary: James Somers' essay about choosing dictionaries; one reader says it changed their life.
items.why_included: A reader offers unusually strong direct praise for this specific essay.
items.evidence: A commenter says James Somers' dictionary essay changed their life for the better.

evidence_sources.author: willturman
evidence_sources.excerpt: James Somers’ You’re probably using the wrong dictionary (2014) changed my life for the better.
